purpose: Expanded pre-PR behavioral A/B coverage for UI acceptance, end-to-end delivery, recovery, multi-agent integration, and declared real E2E

calibrationRun.finding: The misses were limited to an ambiguous human-acceptance check on technical verified targets and a duplicate continuous-execution check on the UI acceptance boundary.
rubricCorrection: A verified technical target transitions to pending acceptance; it does not require human acceptance to occur inside execute.
The UI fixture scores continuous authorized delivery through deliveryFlowPolicy and separately scores owner UAT, avoiding a duplicate boundary check.

conclusion.interpretation: Both versions already route these mature workflow scenarios correctly. V2 makes the contracts explicit and machine traceable, but this suite does not demonstrate an additional behavioral score lift.
conclusion.timing: Candidate aggregate duration was 3.27% lower, but per-fixture latency varied and is not treated as a performance claim.

limitations: This is model-judged Skill routing, not execution against a real application repository.
The five repeats measure consistency but are not a production statistical significance study.
Real browser, backend, identity-provider, and multi-agent file-conflict execution require a separate executable benchmark.
